generation.hypothesis: Thermal aging of as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy will produce a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile response under mechanical loading. Maximum embrittlement near 600 °C will arise from coupled L12 chemical ordering within FCC domains and increased jaggedness of B2/FCC phase boundaries, rather than from conventional grain-boundary impurity segregation. Aging near 750 °C will suppress this ordering and generate ductile transition zones along phase boundaries, thereby restoring ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: The starting material will be as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy containing FCC and B2 phases.
generation.intervention: The alloy will be thermally aged at intermediate temperatures, with controlled comparisons among the as-cast condition, an embrittlement condition near 600 °C, and a recovery condition near 750 °C.
generation.conditions: The critical aging interval will be approximately 550–750 °C, where chemical-ordering kinetics and B2/FCC phase-boundary evolution should be maximized. Mechanical loading will then be used to compare deformation and fracture behavior across aging conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: Near 600 °C, FCC domains will develop enhanced L12 ordering approaching Ni3Al stoichiometry while B2/FCC interfaces will become more jagged. Near 750 °C, L12 ordering should diminish and more ductile transition zones should form along the phase boundaries.
generation.mechanism: Enhanced L12 ordering will raise antiphase-boundary energy and elastic modulus, restrict dislocation cross-slip, and favor planar slip. Dislocation accumulation at sharp tips of jagged B2/FCC boundaries will concentrate stress and trigger plastic instability and crack initiation. Reduced ordering and ductile interfacial transition zones at higher aging temperatures will relax these constraints and permit ductility recovery.
generation.predicted_outcome: Ductility will remain comparatively stable below about 550 °C, fall to a pronounced minimum after aging near 600 °C, and recover substantially near or above 750 °C. The resulting ductile-brittle-ductile transition will track the combined prevalence of highly ordered L12 domains and jagged phase boundaries.
generation.baseline: The mechanistic baseline will be classical thermally induced embrittlement in conventional alloys, in which impurity segregation promotes grain-boundary fracture. The proposed alloy response should instead be phase-boundary- and ordering-mediated without intergranular impurity segregation.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis will apply primarily to mechanically loaded service after aging: below roughly 550 °C no transition is expected, between about 550 and 750 °C a brittle window is expected, and above roughly 750 °C ductile recovery is expected.
generation.uncertainty: The relative contributions of elevated ordering strength and phase-boundary jaggedness may be difficult to separate because both should evolve within the same aging window.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare as-cast material with specimens aged near 600 and 750 °C under equivalent mechanical loading, while characterizing deformation and fracture sites by TKD or TEM.
measurements: Dislocation pile-ups and planar slip within ordered FCC domains
